---
title: "Control System Overview"
---

## Architecture

The prototype is organized into these processing levels:

- the **user computer**, where the PNG pattern is created with the Pattern Editor;
- the **Raspberry Pi**, which implements the user interface, reads and validates PNG patterns, manages process progress and hosts the error-recognition pipeline;
- the **ESP32**, which directly controls the three servomotors and the stepper motor and reads the synchronization microswitch.

```text
Pattern Editor on PC
        │
        │ PNG file on USB flash drive
        ▼
Raspberry Pi + GFX HAT
        │
        │ USB serial protocol: C1, C2, C3, DOWN
        ▼
ESP32
   ├── Servo 1 + 3D-printed arm
   ├── Servo 2 + 3D-printed arm
   ├── Servo 3 + 3D-printed arm
   ├── Stepper + Driver + 3D-printed base
   └── Microswitch ── NEXT event
```

The camera-based error-recognition pipeline also runs on the Raspberry Pi. Its integration with the real servo-control workflow remains a next development step.

## Implemented Control Sequence

```text
User selects a PNG file
        ↓
Raspberry Pi copies and validates the selected pattern
        ↓
User presses AVVIA
        ↓
Raspberry Pi sends the command for the first pixel
        ↓
ESP32 positions one of the three servo arms
        ↓
Microswitch is physically activated
        ↓
ESP32 sends NEXT
        ↓
Raspberry Pi updates progress and sends the next command
        ↓
End of image: DOWN command and completion screen
```
